title: Fuselage — Fwd Cargo Door Surround — Interrupted Seal and Chromate-Free Protection

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Retrofit of the interrupted faying seal and the chromate-free protective scheme at the forward cargo door surround, bringing delivered aircraft to the production standard and lengthening the zonal corrosion inspection interval.

sections.planning_reason: Aircraft delivered before MSN S00992 seal the frame foot to the skin along its full length, so condensate running down the frame web collects behind the foot with no route to the drain path. Corrosion was found behind the foot on twenty-three of ninety-four aircraft sampled above 40 000 flight hours. Left alone the condition grows into a repair, and on three aircraft it grew past the repair scheme. The change also removes the chromated primer, which is being withdrawn under the applicable environmental regulation and is becoming difficult for operators to obtain.
sections.description: The door surround fitting kit and the inboard surround frame sub-assembly are replaced by items with the interrupted seal land machined in, leaving a 12 mm gap at the lowest point of each foot. The joint is re-fastened with the chromate-free washer set and wet-installed with polysulphide. All disturbed surfaces receive the chromate-free primer. Where the survey found material loss inside blend-out limits, the loss is blended and re-protected as part of the same visit.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Do the survey of Service Bulletin SLN-53-1008 first and confirm that the recorded material loss is inside the blend-out limits. Get access to the forward cargo compartment and remove the lower shell lining panels in zones 111 and 121. Do AMM-S-53-21-13-000-001-A to remove the door surround fitting kit D5321131361369 and the inboard frame sub-assembly D5321134517524. Blend out any recorded material loss and do a dye penetrant inspection of each blended area. Clean and dry the faying surfaces. Apply the chromate-free primer to the frame foot and to the skin land, and let it cure. Install the new fitting kit and frame sub-assembly wet with polysulphide, leaving the 12 mm interrupted land clear of sealant. Fasten the joint with washers AES963502K7 and EN736536-59 and plain washers AGS46790-6A to the torque table in the accomplishment instructions. Do a water flow check through the escape route with the aircraft level. Do AMM-S-53-21-13-400-001-A to install the removed items and refit the lining panels. Do the cargo door operational test and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to SOLANO-30 and SOLANO-34 aircraft that are still at the fully sealed frame foot standard. Aircraft from MSN S00992 onward are post-modification in production and must not be modified. Aircraft whose survey found material loss beyond the blend-out limit are outside the scope of this Service Bulletin and need an engineering assessment.
sections.material_note: Kit K5321-1012-01 contains the fitting kit, the frame sub-assembly, the fastener set and the chromate-free primer. Lead time is eighteen weeks. The removed items are not returned. The mass change is a reduction of 0.8 kg per aircraft, which is below the reporting threshold but is recorded for fleet tracking.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled C-check after the survey, or within 36 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

revision_history.reason: Water flow check added after two operators reported the escape route blocked by legacy sealant; torque table corrected at step 8
